AWAKEN · for your approval · 9 November 2026

Powers in Full Voice

A plan to make using powers the best thing in the game. All 63 judged one at a time: what each does today, what it would do, how it would sound and who had it first. Eight new ones held to a higher bar. And everything around them, from how you get a power to how you read it in a fight.

Nothing here is built. I read the code and measured the sounds, but I haven't played a power or heard a clip. Every verdict is mine from reading, so overrule any of them. The tags say which claims come from the code, which from other games and which are my guesses.

You were right about the levels. The ladder stays exactly as it is. Three other things hold the powers back:

  • There's nothing to get good at. 51 of the 63 are one press and a cooldown.
  • They don't know about the game built since. A power has never filled a boss's stance, and casting isn't part of the Ascent's chain.
  • They sound alike and nobody is behind them. 17 calls to one whoosh, and descriptions that name a path instead of a person.

So the plan keeps the 63 and the ladder and adds ten connected changes: a right way to press every power, powers that count on bosses, combinations you find by experimenting, an R key that fills from how you fight, a ground that really moves, a sound pack per power, and a real person behind each one, ending with your own name on your starter.

You also asked for new powers pushed further than anything there now, and for the whole system to be polished. So there are eight new powers, cut down from eighteen, and each one changes something none of the 63 can touch: your size, time, the road, their moves, sound, the horizon, someone else's body and your own past. And there are six changes to the system itself, covering how you get, equip, cast, combine, level and read your powers.

It starts with a playable proof of four powers, and I stop there until you've played it. The new powers come in three waves, with a stop after each.

1What you asked for

Here's how I read it. Tell me if I've got this wrong, because everything below follows from it.

What I took from it
The jobMake using powers extremely fun and satisfying, at every level, for someone who has played a lot.
What's wrongThe first powers were built before most of the game existed and were never revisited. Some are boring. They could be more creative and more technical.
What you want"Holy shit, this is extremely fun and satisfying to use." More progression, more lore.
What you suggestedA sound pack per power, then the powers themselves. I checked whether sound was the main problem. It's one of three.
What you addedNew powers, "really pushed even further" in how enjoyable they are to use and how awesome they look, and "polishing the whole power system up to the maximum". A few astonishing ones beat a long list of decent ones.
What must stayHow they level up. Your saves. Your frame rate. Fair fights.
What I can't checkHow they feel. Only you can do that, so the plan stops early for you to play.

What the bar means, in things you'd notice

StrongWeakUnacceptable
You tell someone about a thing you did with two powers. You could name Railgun with your eyes shut. After a hundred casts you're visibly better and you can hear it. You'd call someone over to see a new power.Bigger numbers, more particles and new sounds laid over the same one press. A new power that's a bigger version of one already there.A power turns into a chore or a quick-time event. Levels you earned vanish. A boss melts in seconds. The frame rate drops. A new power that's only good in a clip.

The success contract

What has to be true
FunEvery power has a better way to press it, and you can tell when you found it.
TruthA power's text says what it does. Numbers come from the simulator, not from me.
EffortNothing to learn before it works. No new menu to manage. A plain cast is today's cast.
ResponseA press answers on the same frame it does today. The Clean ring lands within one server tick, 50 ms.
ControlYou choose your bar and your Way. The notes can be turned off. Nothing changes your loadout for you.
When it can'tA power with nothing to do does something smaller, or says why and costs nothing.
CostAbout 10 MB of sound. No more frame time than the level 5 limit we already test against.

Not part of this

  • Replacing the six-key bar or the 63 powers
  • Permanent allies or followers
  • A new currency, daily lists or announcing bosses
  • Any new block or item
  • The general frame rate pass, which stays parked

Must not get worse

  • The four named levels and the Awakened form
  • Every level, variant and mastery point already earned
  • The Ascent's movement ladder and Weaves
  • Boss fights: the 20% hit cap and fair damage
  • Cinematic frame time

What other games teach OTHER GAMES

Only for questions that change the design. I read reporting and guides, not the original talks, so treat these as pointers.

QuestionWhat I foundHow far it appliesWhat it changes here
Would a timing reward feel good or like homework?Gears of War made each reload a small timing game with a prize. GMTK notes beginners often ignored it. Testing for the 2026 game moved the bar to mid-screen because that's where people used it most (GamingBolt). Its designer later called the multiplayer damage bonus a mistake (Destructoid headline, the rest of the piece was cut off for me).One repeated action in a shooter. We have 63 different ones.The cue goes at the crosshair. A plain cast stays fully fine. The damage bonus doesn't apply against other players.
How many pairings are worth finding?One guide counts 28 Duo Boons in Hades (see Screen Rant and Prima), and Hades II has 37 (Rogue Ranker). Each needs something from both gods.They're rolled per run. You try ours on purpose.24 Duets, each needing only the two powers on your bar.
Rules or a thousand special cases?Breath of the Wild runs a rule-based calculator of states between elements and materials (report on the GDC 2017 talk).An open-world sandbox, and I only read coverage.Six States are general rules. Duets are the named special cases on top.
Can you tell things apart by ear in a busy fight?Overwatch found "the loudest sound wins" and built a system that lifts the biggest threat in the mix, and gave every character its own footsteps (PC Gamer on the GDC 2016 talk).A competitive shooter. I found nothing on how each ability was handled.A mix budget, with your own power and the biggest threat on top.
Timer or meter for the big one?Overwatch fills a meter from damage and healing, with slow passive charge and no timer (wiki, Dexerto).Team PvP. The numbers are community figures.R becomes a gauge, and a slow creep means nobody is locked out.
Fighting beside your own replay: thrilling or a mess?Super Time Force is built on it. Reviewers call it brilliant and also confusing or chaotic (Game Informer, Den of Geek, God is a Geek, GamesRadar).A 2D shooter with many copies at once.Last Time Round is one figure until level 5, in a look you can't mistake for anything else.
How many copied abilities are worth having?Kirby Super Star's team started with more than 40 candidates and kept the strongest (Prima, Nintendo Life). I found no proper design analysis.A much simpler game.I cut hard, and the list of what I cut is on this page.
How long should a press be kept?Smash keeps a press for 9 frames (SmashWiki). Developer blogs give 3 to 5 frames or 80 to 150 ms and warn that long ones feel sticky (Wayline, Bugnet). The sources are uneven.Fighting and action games at 60 frames. Ours is 20 ticks a second.0.15 seconds, which is three ticks. You can try other lengths in section 6.

Strikes.posture for stance, the Weaves' found-not-told pattern, FxDebris and TerrainLedger for the ground, TimeSlow for time, PlaySoundEvent for bending sounds in Flow, audiokit.py and the listening pages for sound, CC0 sources already in the repo so no new download is needed, combat_sim.py for balance, FxStats for frame cost, and Goals for the Tasks page.

3Three ways to do it

A. Repair

New sound pack, powers fill stance, end the dead buttons, remove vanilla leftovers.

About 12 hours. Low risk. Decent to good, but the powers are still one press. It fixes what's wrong without reaching what you asked for.

RECOMMENDED

B. Build underneath

Keep the 63 and the ladder. Add the ten changes, polish the system, rework each power by hand on top of them, and add the eight new ones.

About 100 hours, or about 60 without the new powers. Each piece can be switched off. It's the only option that reaches the bar and keeps the part you like.

C. Start over

Cut to about 30 deep powers with a new key model.

170 hours or more. Breaks the ladder and everyone's saves. Rejected, though its best idea survives: folding the four Architect shapes into one.

What would change my mind: if Stage 0 feels just as good without Clean casts, I'd drop them and move toward A plus the world and sound work. If the ground wave can't hold your frame rate, I'd cut it back to Swift-style dust and keep the rest.

4How it would work

The ten changes PROPOSAL

1Clean casts: every press has a right way

THE PROBLEM

51 of 63 powers are one press and a cooldown. Only three have a release you can time. There's nothing to get better at.

THE CHANGE

Each power gets its own right way, written by hand: a moment, an aim, a position or a move into it. It's listed on every card below. Do it and the cast lands Clean: about 25% more damage, more stance, about 40% of the energy back, and more mastery. The cue is at your crosshair. The server judges it, with two ticks of grace.

WHAT YOU GET

After a hundred casts you're visibly better with a power, and you can hear it.

WHAT IT KEEPS

A cast that isn't Clean does exactly what today's does. Nothing is punished, and a new player can ignore all of it.

THE COST

63 timings to write and balance. The risk is that it feels like a quick-time event.

HOW WE TEST IT

You play four powers in Stage 0 and tell me. The simulator must show no more than about 12% average gain at a 50% Clean rate.

2Powers count on bosses

THE PROBLEM

The powers code has zero calls to the stance system. Blades are the only thing that breaks a boss. The one link is an attuned weapon's touch, worth 6.

THE CHANGE

Every power fills stance by weight through the existing Strikes.posture: Light 3, Medium 6, Heavy 12, Massive 20, Clean half as much again. The same braced and opening rules apply.

WHAT YOU GET

Being a caster finally counts in the fights that matter.

WHAT IT KEEPS

A blade stays the main way. A longsword swung non-stop is about 8 stance a second. A Clean Haymaker every time it's ready is about 3.

THE COST

One more stance source for the boss fights session to allow for. Ranged stance could be abused.

HOW WE TEST IT

combat_sim: breaks per minute no more than 20% above today, tuned on two bosses and checked on bosses it wasn't tuned on.

3No dead buttons

THE PROBLEM

32 places in the catalogue refuse with a red flash: no target 13, blocked 13, and the rest. Dominate and Telekinesis refuse a boss outright, and Gravity Flip skips anything heavy. Worse, a refused cast is normally free, but 14 powers with a wind-up pay first and ignore a later refusal, and at least seven can refuse at that point (Spire, Collapse, Terrain Rip, Thunderclap, Legion, Storm Call, Drone Swarm).

THE CHANGE

An aimed power with nothing to aim at does something smaller. Every power gets a boss version. Wind-up powers check before they charge you.

WHAT YOU GET

A press always answers you.

WHAT IT KEEPS

Real limits stay: energy, cooldown, no room. Those say why and cost nothing.

THE COST

About 30 small behaviours to write.

HOW WE TEST IT

One GameTest casts all 63 at a boss and at nothing. Zero unexplained refusals.

4States and Duets

THE PROBLEM

Seven force reactions exist, mostly against enemy tags, drawn with vanilla particles. Powers barely know each other.

THE CHANGE

Six States show on a creature's body: Lifted, Charged, Burning, Chilled, Held, Read. On top of those, 24 named Duets: two specific powers that make something neither can do alone. You find them by trying things, and they're counted N / ?? like Weaves.

WHAT YOU GET

The stories you tell someone else. Your Well, then your Nova, and the room goes white.

WHAT IT KEEPS

The Weave format, the 20% boss cap, and your freedom to ignore all of it.

THE COST

Stacking is the danger, so every bonus together is capped at about 1.6 times. 24 looks and sounds to write.

HOW WE TEST IT

One test per mechanism. The simulator checks the cap holds in the worst combination.

5Movement powers attack, and casts join the chain

THE PROBLEM

Dash, Leap, Flight, Jet Burst, Snap Cable and others now sit next to the Ascent moves that overlap them. A cast is not a chain link, so the two halves of movement don't know each other.

THE CHANGE

The eight movement powers become attacks that move you. A cast counts as a link in the Ascent's chain, and a long enough chain gives On the Move casts. Wings stay for travel and Flight is for fighting in the air.

WHAT YOU GET

Moving and casting become one thing.

WHAT IT KEEPS

The Ascent's tiers stay the Ascent's. Nothing on its ladder moves.

THE COST

Eight reworks. Chains will reach further, so air fights need a balance check.

HOW WE TEST IT

A test that a cast links through AscentServer.link, and you judge the feel.

6The R key fills from how you fight

THE PROBLEM

Ultimates sit on a 60 second timer. There are seven, six only come from a Path, and four families have none, so R is empty for hours.

THE CHANGE

R becomes a gauge. Clean casts, Duets, finishers and kills fill it, and it creeps up on its own so nobody is ever locked out. No energy cost. Your first ultimate is the reward for the D Proving, chosen from what you've actually done.

WHAT YOU GET

The big moment comes when you've earned it, and it comes early enough to matter.

WHAT IT KEEPS

Path signatures still come from Paths.

THE COST

Every ultimate needs rebalancing.

HOW WE TEST IT

Simulator: about 90 seconds of good fighting fills it, about three minutes of sloppy fighting still does.

7The world answers

THE PROBLEM

Almost everything is drawn on top of the world. The tools for more already exist (FxDebris reads real blocks, TerrainLedger restores them, TimeSlow zones) and go mostly unused. Some powers still use vanilla particles, which breaks your look rule.

THE CHANGE

The ground really comes up, in whatever you're standing on. Beam leaves a scorch. Frost freezes real water for a while. The Well pulls loose things and bends shots. Charge runs through water and metal. Flow slows every new sound through the game's own sound event. Every vanilla particle goes.

WHAT YOU GET

It stops looking like an add-on.

WHAT IT KEEPS

Your frame budget. Ground pieces stay inside the existing debris cap (160 full, 64 reduced, 0 minimal). Everything put back afterwards.

THE COST

The hardest look work in the plan. Bending light round a Well would be new Lens work and is only a guess until tried.

HOW WE TEST IT

Stage 0 proves the ground wave first, with FxStats on the Mac.

8A sound pack for every power

THE PROBLEM

172 sound files, and 17 calls to one whoosh. Haymaker and Railgun share a charge. Gravity Well is silent for most of its life. You haven't heard most of them in game.

THE CHANGE

Each power gets a charge or wind, a release, an impact, a tail, a Clean layer and a level 5 layer, two versions of each. Each family gets its own instruments. A sung Choir layer comes in at level 5. A mix budget keeps your own power and the biggest threat on top.

WHAT YOU GET

You could close your eyes and name the power.

WHAT IT KEEPS

Today's sounds. Old files stay in place until you've passed the new one.

THE COST

About 340 sound events and 700 short files, about 10 MB. I can't hear any of them, so your ears are the gate.

HOW WE TEST IT

A listening page per family: Today, New, New in the mix, Keep or Redo on each. Loudness measured to within 1.5 dB.

9Readings: every power has a person

THE PROBLEM

The descriptions say things like a path's signature or a latent gift. The story already has the answer: the Choir reads people and plays back who they could be. Nothing connects that to your powers.

THE CHANGE

A Power Core is a recording the Choir took of a real person. The Deep is full of people who had them, which is why Lords drop Cores. Each power has a first bearer, one line when you learn it and one more per level. The Journal keeps them in The Choir's Record. At level 5 of your starter you find a second name on the reading.

WHAT YOU GET

Levelling up a power turns into finding out who they were, and then who you are.

WHAT IT KEEPS

The ladder. No Echoes and no allies. The System's plain bracketed voice.

THE COST

About 300 short lines to write and read aloud.

HOW WE TEST IT

You read them all in one file before they ship.

10Progress you earn by playing

THE PROBLEM

Cores come at random by rank, so there's nothing to go looking for, and powers have no tab on the Tasks page. The ladder itself is good, so it stays exactly as it is.

THE CHANGE

Gate themes and Lords lean toward the families they've swallowed, with about a third staying random. At level 5 the System reads how you actually used the power and offers up to three ways to keep it, with the evidence. You pick one and can change it. New Powers tab through Goals.

WHAT YOU GET

You can hunt a power, and level 5 is about you.

WHAT IT KEEPS

All four levels, the 7,000 / 13,000 / 32,000 / 50,000 mastery, and every level already earned.

THE COST

One more choice at level 5, though it's optional and reversible.

HOW WE TEST IT

Ledger and Goals tests. Your Way only uses real counters, so a new player sees no made-up evidence.

The six States

Liftedfrom Kinetic, GravityIn the air and helpless. Any hit slams it down hard for extra stance.
Chargedfrom Charge powersThe next hit arcs to the nearest thing. Water and metal carry it further.
Burningfrom Heat powersA cold hit makes steam. A heavy hit spreads the fire.
Chilledfrom Frost powersThree layers freeze it. A heavy hit shatters what's frozen.
Heldfrom Tethers, grips, ordersIt can't get away. Your next hit lands from the blind side.
Readfrom Mind powersYou can see its next blow. Your next cast on it lands Clean.

The whole system PROPOSAL

The ten changes are about what a power does. These six are about everything around it, from the moment you pick up a Core.

11Get: having a power should be an event

THE PROBLEM

Right-clicking a Core teaches the power that instant: a bloom, a chord and a window (Powers.useCore). There's nothing to do with it yet. A Core of a power that's already mastered just says so and stays in your hand.

THE CHANGE

Hold use for a second and the Core cracks in your hand. The first Reading plays and the power goes on a free key if there is one. Your first press is free and can't be refused, so you feel it on the spot. A Core of a mastered power can be poured into another power of the same family as mastery.

WHAT YOU GET

Getting a power is a moment, you've used it within five seconds, and no Core is ever wasted.

WHAT IT KEEPS

The same Cores and ladder, sneak-use to swap variants, and the Starter's three cards.

THE COST

A short hold and a crack to make.

HOW WE TEST IT

GameTest: a mastered Core gives mastery and never a level, and the free press spends nothing.

12Equip: your bar should be something you build

THE PROBLEM

One set of six keys (Loadout), so changing build means re-slotting by hand. The card shows cost and cooldown but no damage, and nothing says what a power is good with. Every power sits in one grid of 22-pixel icons.

THE CHANGE

Three saved sets that you name, swapped from the K page or a held key once you're out of a fight. The card gains damage (PowerPreviews already works it out for Cores), the right way, the Duets you've found, the Reading and a Try button that shuts the menu and gives you one free press. Sort by family, level or what a power does.

WHAT YOU GET

A set for Lords, a set for travel, and a reason to own more than six powers.

WHAT IT KEEPS

Click then press a key, your own bindings, and the ladder on the card.

THE COST

Cooldowns belong to the power and never the set, so swapping can't reset them. Loadout schema 4 carries the sets.

HOW WE TEST IT

A schema 3 save loads as set one. Swapping during a fight is refused.

13Cast: stop throwing presses away

THE PROBLEM

A press a moment before the cooldown ends is refused and forgotten (ClientCasting.press). The reason appears in small type beside the hotbar with no sound. Nothing shows where an area power will land.

THE CHANGE

A press buffer: in the last 0.15 seconds of a cooldown or during another power's wind-up, your press is kept and fires the moment it can. Hold the key on the dozen or so powers that land somewhere to see where, with a ring in the power's own look, and let go to cast. A tap still casts at once. The reason moves to your crosshair, once a second, with a low thud that differs for no energy, not ready and no room.

WHAT YOU GET

Powers stop eating your inputs, and you know where the big ones will land.

WHAT IT KEEPS

A tap is the same as today. Movement prediction and second presses are untouched, and the six held powers keep hold as their charge.

THE COST

A buffer must never fire something you've changed your mind about, so any other power key or a dodge clears it.

HOW WE TEST IT

GameTest: a buffered press fires once and spends once. You judge the feel at Stage 2.

14Combine: help you play the Duets you've found

THE PROBLEM

Powers combine in seven small ways that nothing on screen shows (ForceInteractions). The plan adds States and Duets, and the screen has to keep up.

THE CHANGE

When a creature has a State that one of your keys can use in a Duet you've already found, that key shows a small glint. Duets you haven't found never show. The first time you find one, the moment slows for a quarter of a second and its name goes up once, large. States sit on the creature's body and on its lock-on panel, and a party member's count too.

WHAT YOU GET

You can play Duets on purpose once you've found them, and finding them stays a surprise.

WHAT IT KEEPS

The N / ?? list, and the rule that nothing tells you what you haven't found.

THE COST

A few more small things on the bar, so they only show in a fight.

HOW WE TEST IT

A test that an unfound Duet never sends a glint.

15Level: leave it alone and add a little

THE PROBLEM

You like this and you're right to. In a fight it's a short sting and the moment waits. When it's calm you get the bloom, a chord and a window naming the step (Evolution), and the slot's frame grows. Two gaps: you can't see mastery while fighting, and the window tells you about the new step without letting you feel it.

THE CHANGE

Everything stays. The window gains a Try It press: your next cast of that power is free and shows the new step. When you're a few uses from the next level, the slot's frame draws a thin line round itself. The window also carries the next line of the Reading.

WHAT YOU GET

The moment you level up, you get to use what you just earned.

WHAT IT KEEPS

All of it: the steps, the frames, the sting and the moment, and mastery thresholds.

THE COST

Almost nothing.

HOW WE TEST IT

A test that Try It is free once and only once per level.

16Read: you should be able to fight without looking down

THE PROBLEM

The bar is 20-pixel slots beside the hotbar, a long way from where you're looking. A cooldown is a dark shade that shrinks, and when it ends nothing happens at all, no flash and no sound. Energy is a 3-pixel bar. Slot edges stay grey unless a power is running.

THE CHANGE

A slot that comes back gives a bright glint and a quiet tick pitched to its family, and a full R gets a bigger one. The cooldown becomes a bright sweep you can catch from the corner of your eye. Family colours on every edge. A ghost on the energy bar shows what your last press cost. Two thin arcs at the crosshair for energy and R, only during a fight, with a setting to turn them off.

WHAT YOU GET

You know what's ready by hearing it.

WHAT IT KEEPS

Frames that grow with level, the beating outline for a second press, F1 hiding it all, and the narrow-screen layout.

THE COST

Clutter is the risk, and you approved Clear Screen for a reason. So nothing near the crosshair shows outside a fight, and it has to fit with the aim dot (SPEC 40.5).

HOW WE TEST IT

CI tour shots at your MacBook's size, then you play.

The rules it must keep

StepWhat happens
TriggerA key press on one of the six slots, exactly as today.
ReadsThe power, its level and variant, your aim, what's under your aim, your movement, what's already on the target, your energy and cooldown.
DoesSecond press? Can it act, and which version? Pay. Wind up. Release and judge Clean. Hit, stance, State. Duet check. Gauge, mastery, counters.
You seeThe effect, the Clean ring, the State on the creature, and the first time you find a Duet, a toast.
AllowedDamage and stance inside the caps, temporary terrain through the ledger, short-lived summons.
SavedLoadout schema 4 only, with your sets. Nothing mid-fight is saved.
When it can'tNo energy, on cooldown, no room: it says why and costs nothing.

These are always true

  • A cast that isn't Clean equals today's cast
  • The server decides damage and Clean, never the client
  • The 20% boss hit cap stands, and all bonuses together stop at about 1.6 times
  • Every terrain change puts itself back unless it's something you built
  • No permanent allies, only short-lived summons and decoys
  • No power moves, stops or controls another player
  • With a change's setting off, the game behaves as it did without it

When two things clash

  • Boss cap beats the 1.6 cap, which beats any single bonus
  • Two time effects: the stronger one wins, they never stack
  • A Duet needs both powers from you or your party
  • Clean is judged at release, so the wind-up can't be gamed by a late aim
  • The Ascent's ladder always wins over a power that overlaps it
  • A kept press is cleared by any other power key or a dodge

Multiplayer and boundaries

  • The server is in charge, and looks and sound stay on the client
  • Duets work across a party
  • Dominate, Echo Swap and time stop never touch players
  • The existing limit on aim-bending against people stays
  • Clean's damage bonus doesn't apply against players
  • None of the eight new powers can stop, grab or enter another player
  • No new data leaves the game

Frame rate and cost

  • Limit we already test against: level 5 costs at most 0.5 ms typical and 1 ms worst over level 1
  • Ground pieces stay inside the existing cap
  • About 10 MB of sound on top of the current 2.2 MB
  • A command prints each power's Clean rate, Duets found and stance dealt
  • Titan and the Clock add no meshes. Road Ahead is a drawn strip with no block changes. Toll uses the screen pass power impacts already have. The Long Cut is the only new power that changes many blocks
  • Frame tests run on your Mac when it's quiet, under slot.sh

5Eight new powers

You asked for new powers pushed further than anything in the catalogue, both to use and to look at, and you said a few astonishing ones beat a long list of decent ones. I agree. So I wrote down what a new power has to do, came up with eighteen, and kept the ones that passed.

The test each one had to pass

1
Nothing else does it

It has to do a kind of thing the catalogue doesn't do at all. A bigger version of something we already have doesn't count.

2
You'd call someone over

One moment you'd want to show another person, and it has to look as good from outside as from inside.

3
The hundredth time is better

You get better at it. A power that's at its best the first time you press it fails.

4
It belongs here

It comes from something the story already says, and you get it by doing something the world can remember.

5
It can really be built

The parts exist in the code or a short named test can prove them, and it stays fair, safe for multiplayer and inside the frame budget.

The eight that passed don't overlap. Each one changes something none of the 63 can touch:

Your sizeTitanTimeStopped ClockThe roadRoad AheadTheir movesSay It BackSoundTollThe horizonThe Long CutSomeone else's bodyBorrowed BodyYour own pastLast Time Round

Where each one comes in

YOUR SIZE

Titan

Kinetic · Ultimate, on R · wave 1

The R key is full. You grow, as big as the place allows, up to five times your height: nine blocks on open ground. For twelve seconds your swing sweeps a whole room, Z is a stomp that sends the ground out in a wave, and X picks up anything smaller than you and throws it.

WHY IT'S A THRILL

The fight changes scale in a second. The thing you were dodging is at your waist. You can feel your weight: every step rocks the camera and throws up real dirt, and the trees you walk through go down.

WHAT ONLY IT DOES

Nothing else in the catalogue changes your size. It's also the only power that gives your other keys new jobs while it lasts.

HOW IT LOOKS

You stay yourself, armour and all, only huge, with hot orange seams at the joints. The growth comes in three heaves. Your shadow falls across the ground ahead of you and mobs look up.

HOW IT SOUNDS

A creak like old timber taking load as you grow. Sub-bass footsteps you feel more than hear. Your own breath and your own power sounds drop about an octave while you're big, and come back up when you shrink.

THE RIGHT WAY

Time your first stomp to land on the last heave of the growth. The wave goes twice as far.

ON A BOSS

A boss can't be picked up. X shoves it instead and takes a big bite of stance. Every hit still stops at the 20% cap.

KEEPING IT FAIR

Other players are never grabbed. In a cave or a gate you only grow as far as the roof allows, and if a roof closes in you shrink to fit, so you can't get stuck.

HOW YOU EARN IT

Offered at the D Proving if most of what you've done with powers so far is Kinetic. Anyone else can get its Core from the gates that lean Kinetic, once Cores have sources.

Lv 2 · Longer StrideYou cover ground at the speed your legs look like they should.
Lv 3 · UprootedX can tear up a tree or a boulder and throw that.
Lv 4 · Walking EarthquakeEach step ripples the ground and trips small things near your feet.
Lv 5 · The Whole HeightAwakened. Seven times your height on open ground, and the first stomp cracks the land out to 30 blocks.
[Bram Okoye was five foot two and lifted a bus off a child outside Carillon station. He weighs a lot more in the Choir's copy than he did in life. So will you.]
SEEN IN CODE The game's size attribute goes up to 16 times and we already use it on mobs (MobScaling). Step height, reach and jump are attributes too.
MY GUESS How the camera and first-person arms behave at five times size. One short test.
About 3 hours, with its sound pack, ladder, icon and tests.
TIME

Stopped Clock

Velocity · Ultimate, on R · wave 1

One tick of a clock, then nothing. Every creature near you stops dead, the colour drains out of the world and only you and your own powers keep theirs. For three seconds you walk around a fight that's holding its breath. Arrows hang where they were. Everything you do is held: your shots leave your hand and stop a metre out, and your hits pile up on whatever you struck. Then the clock starts again and all of it lands in the same instant.

WHY IT'S A THRILL

It's three seconds of planning inside a fight, and then one enormous payoff that you built. You walk round a frozen boss laying shots around it like a firing squad. The better you compose those three seconds, the bigger the one frame at the end.

WHAT ONLY IT DOES

Flow and Foresight slow things down. This is the only power where what you do waits, so you're stacking up a single moment instead of hitting things in turn.

HOW IT LOOKS

On your screen every creature freezes mid-step, animation included. Held shots stay lit and slowly turn. A thin white mark appears for each hit waiting on a target. On release: one frame of white, then full colour comes back all at once.

HOW IT SOUNDS

The tick. Then almost nothing: the whole mix drops to a low hum and your footsteps are the only clear thing. Each held hit adds one quiet note to a rising stack. On release the stack and every impact play as a single hit with a long tail.

THE RIGHT WAY

Land your last held hit in the final half second. A full stack ends with a bigger release.

ON A BOSS

Bosses don't stop. They drag at a quarter speed so a fight stays a fight. All your held hits on one boss count as a single hit for the 20% cap, and the release is worth Massive stance.

KEEPING IT FAIR

Other players never stop. A held hit is dropped if its target has left the area. If you die or log out, nothing is held any more and the world starts again.

HOW YOU EARN IT

Offered at the D Proving if you mostly fight with Velocity powers. Everyone else earns it by taking Flow or Foresight to level 5: stay in slow time long enough and one day it stops.

Lv 2 · Another SecondFour seconds, and you can hold one more shot.
Lv 3 · Pushed AsideSlap a hanging arrow or bolt and it goes where you sent it when the clock restarts.
Lv 4 · Everything At OnceHeld hits also set off any State on the target, all together.
Lv 5 · NoonAwakened. Six seconds. Rain stops in the air, and for a second after the release nothing near you can cast.
[Yusra Demir mended clocks. When the Choir asked her what she wanted, she said one more minute with the shop open. She's still in it. It's still that minute.]
SEEN IN CODE TimeSlow already cancels creatures' ticks near you. The client has its own freeze switch (TickRateManager), and the renderer already honours it for every creature, so only you see the full stop.
MY GUESS Vanilla particles and rain aren't covered by that switch. Our own effects can hang. The rest needs trying.
About 4 hours, with its sound pack, ladder, icon and tests.
THE ROAD

Road Ahead

Architect · Movement, on Left Alt · wave 2

Hold Left Alt and start running. A strip of hard light lays itself down in front of your feet, tile by tile, wherever you're looking. Run off a cliff and it carries on. Look up and it climbs. Lean into a turn and it banks. It stays behind you for ten seconds and then falls away in pieces.

WHY IT'S A THRILL

It's a line you draw across the sky with your own body. There's speed to build on the way down and speed to lose on the way up, so a long run is a real piece of driving. You can jump off it, drop, and land back on your own road further along.

WHAT ONLY IT DOES

Every other way of moving is a burst or a hover. This one is continuous and you steer it, and it leaves something behind that's still there when you look back. Other players can run on it too.

HOW IT LOOKS

Warm blueprint gold. The tiles snap into place with a small overlap, so it reads as something being built very fast. The edges glow where you've just been and cool as they age. At the end of its life each tile drops and rings off the next.

HOW IT SOUNDS

A ratchet that clicks once per tile and speeds up with you until it blurs into one rising note. Creaks on the tight bends. A wooden boom as you pass twice sprint speed.

THE RIGHT WAY

Come off the end of the road with speed and land on a ledge or a creature. The speed carries into the Ascent's next move.

ON A BOSS

Lay it round a boss and you can stay out of reach, but a hit needs a landing. Coming off the end onto a boss is a drop attack that counts your speed.

KEEPING IT FAIR

It costs energy for every second you're climbing, less on the flat and none going downhill. Run out on the way up and the tiles ahead flicker for a second before you drop, so you always get a warning.

HOW YOU EARN IT

Reach the top of an Elder Colossus or a Lumen Spire on foot. The Core waits in the cache beside the crown.

Lv 2 · BankingNo speed lost in the turns.
Lv 3 · Two LanesWide enough to turn round on, and a friend can keep up beside you.
Lv 4 · KerbSmall creatures that touch it get tripped.
Lv 5 · The Long RoadAwakened. It stays for thirty seconds, and going downhill pays energy back.
[Pia Lund carried the post on foot between the hill towns. In the last winter she got tired of waiting for roads. There's a line of frost across the pass that still hasn't melted.]
SEEN IN CODE Water Run already holds you up with client physics, and the Runner's hang already passes the game's floating check. A road is a list of points plus a drawn strip, with no block changes at all.
MY GUESS Whether it feels like driving or like sliding on glass. That's the whole power, so it gets its own test.
About 4 hours, with its sound pack, ladder, icon and tests.
THEIR MOVES

Say It Back

Mind · Active, on Z X C or V · wave 2

When a boss or Lord throws a big move at you and you dodge it, deflect it or read it cleanly, this key takes a copy for fifteen seconds. Its icon changes to show what you've got. Press it and you do that move: its shape, its reach, its colours and its own sound, from your own hands, aimed where you're looking.

WHY IT'S A THRILL

The biggest thing in the room just tried to kill you with it, and now it's yours. Every boss gives you something different, so this power plays differently in every fight you'll ever have.

WHAT ONLY IT DOES

It's the one power whose content comes from the enemy: 497 moves across 47 bosses, 47 of them signatures. It's also the answer to Fights That Read You. They read what you've started. This lets you read them back.

HOW IT LOOKS

The copy is made of glass in the boss's own colours. A blow comes out as a huge glass limb the size of the boss's own, swinging from your shoulder through the real arc of the move. A ring of bolts is the boss's own bolts. A slam is its own crater, lit from inside.

HOW IT SOUNDS

The move's own sound, taken up three semitones and dried out, with a glass ringing on top. You recognise it instantly, and it sounds like a bad impression of the thing that scared you.

THE RIGHT WAY

Say it back while the boss is still recovering from the original. It lands Clean and staggers harder.

ON A BOSS

The damage is yours, worked out from your own level and never the boss's. A boss hit by its own signature takes double stance and can't use that move again for 20 seconds.

KEEPING IT FAIR

Moves that make no sense in your hands get a translation: a summon gives you one short-lived copy of yourself, a guard gives you a perfect guard for a second, a heal heals you a little. It never copies another player.

HOW YOU EARN IT

The first time you cleanly answer a Lord's signature move at rank B or higher, the System offers it.

Lv 2 · Long MemoryIt holds a copy for thirty seconds.
Lv 3 · Two at OnceIt holds two moves on one key, and each press spends the oldest.
Lv 4 · Word for WordSignature moves come out at the boss's full size.
Lv 5 · Say It FirstAwakened. If a boss starts a move you've said back before, pressing now beats it to the punch, cancels its move and takes a huge bite of stance.
[Ines Okafor could repeat anything she'd heard once, in the voice she heard it in. Mostly she used it to win arguments with her mother. The Choir read her for eleven minutes, and she read it back.]
SEEN IN CODE Every boss move is data (KitMoves): hit shapes, timing, sounds and what kind of ability it is. The 25 ability kinds are a fixed list (Ability.Kind), so one set of player versions covers every boss.
MY GUESS More than half the moves (265 of 497) are body blows, so the glass limb has to look right. One boss in a test will show it.
About 5 hours, with its sound pack, ladder, icon and tests.
SOUND

Toll

Spirit · Active, on Z X C or V · wave 2

You strike the air with your open hand. Every sound in the world drops away. Half a second later a bell goes off that's bigger than anything you've heard in this game, and you can see the sound leave: a thin gold ring going out across the land, through hills, out past where you can see. The Deep's creatures reel. And any bell you haven't found that's within earshot answers, faintly, from where it is.

WHY IT'S A THRILL

The silence first. Then the size of it. You stand on a hill and watch a ring cross the valley, and then from somewhere out there you hear one small note come back.

WHAT ONLY IT DOES

It's the only power that's as much for the map as for the fight, and the only one where the sound is the weapon. It also ties straight into the game's main goal.

HOW IT LOOKS

A hair-thin gold ring that bends the view as it passes, shakes dust off every surface it crosses and lifts the birds. An answering bell shows as a small ring on the horizon in the right direction.

HOW IT SOUNDS

Built from the bell work already in the game. The silence is the existing muffle system taken nearly all the way down, so the first thing you hear is your own hand landing.

THE RIGHT WAY

Strike within a beat of a real bell ringing near you and yours takes its note and goes out twice as far.

ON A BOSS

Deep and Hollow bosses take Massive stance and lose their next move. Everything else takes a Medium hit to stance. The Deep can't stand it, and the rest just don't like it.

KEEPING IT FAIR

Reach runs from 60 blocks at 50 bells up to 200 at 100. A setting keeps the silence from being total for anyone who finds it uncomfortable, and subtitles give the direction of an answering bell.

HOW YOU EARN IT

Ring 50 of the Hundred. It comes from the bells themselves, and its reach grows with every one you ring after that.

Lv 2 · CarryingThe answering bell is louder, and you can tell how far away it is.
Lv 3 · Held NoteHold it and the silence lasts three seconds. Nothing caught in it can cast.
Lv 4 · Second StrokePress again as the ring fades to send a second one.
Lv 5 · Full PealAwakened. Three strokes, and every bell you've rung within reach sounds along with them.
[Marta Selby rang the noon bell in Carillon for forty years and was late exactly once. She was on the stairs when the bells stopped. She's still on the stairs.]
SEEN IN CODE Bells.count gives your number. Soundscape.muffle already takes the world's sound down for dreams. A screen-bending pass already exists for power impacts (FxScreen).
MY GUESS How far out the ring still reads. Far Sight's distant land may hide it.
About 4 hours, with its sound pack, ladder, icon and tests.
THE HORIZON

The Long Cut

Energy · Ultimate, on R · wave 2

Hold R. A hair-thin white line draws itself across the ground from your feet to as far as you can see, following the land over hills and across valleys. You can sweep it left and right. Let go and for half a second nothing happens. Then the land opens along that line, from your feet to the horizon, in one travelling wave. Anything on it is cut. Trees drop in. Over the next half minute it closes again, from the far end back toward you.

WHY IT'S A THRILL

You changed the view. From a hilltop you can see the whole of what you just did, a straight line through everything for 200 blocks. The half second of nothing between letting go and the land opening is the best part.

WHAT ONLY IT DOES

The longest reach any power has today is 48 blocks. This one reaches the horizon, and its effect is the landscape.

HOW IT LOOKS

A cut three blocks wide and up to twenty deep. The inside walls glow like cooling steel and steam comes off any water that falls in. Near you the blocks are really gone. Far away it's drawn on the land as a dark seam with hot edges, which costs almost nothing.

HOW IT SOUNDS

A rising glass tone that stops dead. Half a second of nothing. Then a tearing sound that starts at your feet and travels away from you, and the far end reaches you late, the way thunder does.

THE RIGHT WAY

Let go in the brief moment the line goes gold at full length.

ON A BOSS

One Massive hit and Massive stance, only if the line crosses it, inside the 20% cap. Worth aiming.

KEEPING IT FAIR

It never touches anything anyone has built, any village, or any block that can't be put back. In a gate the floor holds and you get the line of damage with no canyon. Everything comes back on its own, even after a crash.

HOW YOU EARN IT

The first S-rank Lord you finish with an Energy power on your bar hands you its Core.

Lv 2 · Steady HandA wider sweep while you hold.
Lv 3 · Second LinePress again to cross it with another.
Lv 4 · Deep CutCreatures caught in it are stuck for two seconds.
Lv 5 · Both WaysAwakened. It goes out in front of you and behind you at once.
[Tomasz Ilyin was told to draw a line on the map to show where the evacuation would stop. He had a Halo gun and a bad sense of humour. Nobody crossed that line for nine years.]
SEEN IN CODE TerrainLedger takes blocks out and puts them back, even after a crash, and refuses protected ground. Real blocks only within about 40 of you, spread over a second. Soundscape.muffle does the silence.
MY GUESS The frame cost of even that many block changes on your Mac. And whole trees: you told me nothing should float, so a cut tree has to go down in one piece.
About 5 hours, with its sound pack, ladder, icon and tests.
SOMEONE ELSE'S BODY

Borrowed Body

Mind · Ultimate, on R · wave 3

Press R looking at a creature. Your body kneels where it stands with its eyes shut, and you're inside the creature. You walk on its legs at its height. Left click swings what it swings, and Z, X, C and V are its own moves. Press R at another creature and you jump across, and the one you left falls over.

WHY IT'S A THRILL

You get to be the monster. A ten-block beast rampaging through its own friends, then you hop to the thing on the roof that was about to shoot you. Chaining hops through a whole room is the skill, with your real body waiting, helpless, somewhere behind you.

WHAT ONLY IT DOES

Everything else changes what your character does. This changes who your character is. No other power hands you another creature's height, speed and moves.

HOW IT LOOKS

A thin pink thread runs from your kneeling body to the creature's head, tighter and brighter the further you go. The camera drops or rises to its real eye height. The creature you're wearing has a pink light where its eyes are.

HOW IT SOUNDS

Your own breath, small and far behind you, under the creature's heartbeat and all its real sounds right up close. When your body is hit you hear it from the wrong direction.

THE RIGHT WAY

Hop in the moment the creature you're in would die. You keep the time you had left, plus two seconds.

ON A BOSS

You can't get into a boss. Press R at one and you reach in for a moment: it drops its next move and stumbles a step.

KEEPING IT FAIR

Twelve seconds at most. Your real body can be hit, and one hit pulls you back. You can't go further than 48 blocks from it. Never other players, and never anyone who lives at your Hearth. Kills count for half the mastery.

HOW YOU EARN IT

Take Dominate to level 5. You've been giving orders to creatures for long enough that one day you go in yourself.

Lv 2 · Better FitSixteen seconds.
Lv 3 · Quick HandsA hop costs no time at all.
Lv 4 · Someone WatchingYour kneeling body gets a dome that takes the first hit.
Lv 5 · Full OccupancyAwakened. Whatever you were last inside keeps fighting for you for ten seconds after you leave.
[Ren Takeda looked after other people's dogs. He could tell you exactly what one was about to do. The Choir found out why, and then nobody could find Ren. Keep your own body somewhere safe.]
SEEN IN CODE Handing the camera to another entity is already done for the opening, the Forge and the map (setCameraEntity). The moves of every boss-grade creature are data. Dominate already takes creatures over through Allies.
MY GUESS This is the riskiest of the eight. Driving a creature by hand instead of by its brain hasn't been tried here. It gets its own test, and if that's poor I'll say so and drop it.
About 8 hours, with its sound pack, ladder, icon and tests.
YOUR OWN PAST

Last Time Round

The Signal · Ultimate, on R · wave 3

Press R. The last eight seconds of your fight are pulled out of you. A white figure with gold seams and no face stands up where you were eight seconds ago and does exactly what you did: the same steps, the same powers, at the same moments, at 60% strength. Meanwhile you're free to do something else.

WHY IT'S A THRILL

You get to fight beside yourself, and you can plan for it. Set up a Well, throw a punch, press R, and spend the next eight seconds doing what your past self couldn't. When your old Well meets your new Nova, that's a Duet, and you played both halves.

WHAT ONLY IT DOES

It's the only power whose effect is whatever you just did. Play well and it's devastating. Play badly and you get to watch yourself do it again. It can't be the same twice.

HOW IT LOOKS

The same body as the Last Loop, at your size. Just before it stands, the path it's about to walk lights up from the far end as a thin gold line, exactly as the boss did it to you. Every power in its hands is white and gold instead of its family's colour, so you never mistake it for yourself.

HOW IT SOUNDS

Your own sounds, half a step lower and with a long tail, arriving very slightly late. A soft bell ticks off the eight seconds.

THE RIGHT WAY

Press it the moment you land a Clean cast. The figure starts with your rhythm and its first cast is Clean too.

ON A BOSS

Real damage and real stance at 60%, inside every cap. Bosses can't read it, because it isn't deciding anything.

KEEPING IT FAIR

It repeats what your powers did. It never builds, never summons and never moves land. Only one at a time until level 5, and it can't record itself.

HOW YOU EARN IT

Beat the Last Loop, the final Proving. It kneels, lays its blade down, and this is what it leaves.

Lv 2 · Ten SecondsTen seconds of you instead of eight.
Lv 3 · Step BackPress R again while it's out and you swap places with it, wherever it's got to.
Lv 4 · Word for WordFull strength if you were Clean when you pressed it.
Lv 5 · Every Time RoundAwakened. Two figures: the last eight seconds, and the eight before.
[That was you. You got further than this once, and everything you've got, you brought back with you. There's no other name on this one.]
SEEN IN CODE The Last Loop boss already keeps your path, a sample every two ticks. EchoGhost already walks a recorded path wearing your skin. Power hits run through one place (Combat.hurt) and effects through another (Fx), so the figure repeats the results and never has to re-run 63 powers' code.
MY GUESS Whether repeating results looks right when the target has moved. A test with four powers will show it.
About 5 hours, with its sound pack, ladder, icon and tests.

Play with the strangest one

Last Time Round is the hardest one to picture, so here's a toy of it. Move around, hit the boss, then press the button. Everything you did in the last eight seconds comes back and plays beside you, so whatever you do next is on top of it. This is only a drawing of the idea. It isn't the game.

Move, click at the boss, then press this (or R).

What didn't make it, and why

Two of these were in my first draft of this plan. Say if you'd have any of them back.

IdeaWhat it would doWhy it's out
Nobody HomeIn my first draft. For six seconds nothing near you remembers you're there.Cloak already does nearly this. It's a good trick, and it isn't a new kind of thing.
Second TryIn my first draft. Go back to where you stood four seconds ago with the health you had then.Last Time Round says the same thing better, and its Step Back level gives you the best part. Rewinding health sits badly with fair damage.
UnderSwim through solid ground and come up beneath someone.The game resets a player's collision every tick, and a camera inside stone is a rendering job of its own. Lovely, and too much risk for now.
OrbitLock on to a boss and circle it like a moon, faster and faster, then fling off.A great feel, and better as a level 5 Way for Gravity Well than as its own power.
Two DoorsPlace two linked doors and send anything through.Without seeing through them it's half the idea, and a live view through a door is too much for your frame rate.
Down Is Over TherePick any wall and make it your floor.The game's physics knows up and down and nothing else. It would mean rebuilding how the player moves.
EclipseCover the sun and fight at midnight in the middle of the day.Looks wonderful, but underneath it's a colour grade and a damage buff. Better as Legion's Awakened look.
Thousand CutsThe world stops and you flash through everyone with camera cuts.Hundred Palms and Lightning Step already own this.
CometGo up out of sight and come down as a meteor.The Ascent's Judgement Fall is this, and the rule is that the Ascent's moves stay the Ascent's.
Second WindAt zero health you get six seconds to earn it back.It muddies fair damage and the way dying already works in gates and dreams.

Dov Harlan

Learned[Dov Harlan threw one punch in his whole life that mattered. The Choir kept a copy of it. That's what you're holding.]
Level 2[He was a dock worker. The man he hit was the foreman who'd been shorting everyone's pay.]
Level 3[The foreman lived. Dov went to prison for it, and the docks paid everyone what they were owed the next week.]
Level 4[He never threw another punch. When the Choir asked him why, he said he hadn't needed to.]
Level 5[I looked at this reading again. There are two names on it. His, and under that, yours. You picked this one last time too.]

That last line appears only on the power you chose as your starter. It agrees with what the story already says: the Signal is you, from an earlier loop.

LEVEL 5: YOUR WAY, FOR A HAYMAKER

[I've been watching how you use this. There are three ways it could go from here. You can change your mind later.]

Skybreaker
Thrown from the air, it drives them into the ground and leaves a crater.
You threw 38% of them from the air.
Counterpunch
Thrown into a blow that's landing, it hits twice as hard and stops the blow.
71% of yours landed Clean.
Single Combat
With only one enemy near you, the charge is a third faster.
64% were on one target.
